sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. 2020. Harmony and disharmony in Mbat (Jarawan Bantu) verbs. Linguistique et Langues Africaines 6: 43-72. doi:10.4000/lla.289
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 2 (pp. 50-51): Mbat tonal system 'still a work in progress'; three surface tone levels H, M, L (plus a Super-Low on the Habitual suffix), preliminary evidence for a four-way underlying tonal contrast plus toneless TBUs; fn. 4: no tonal alternations on stems under suffixation.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. Jarawan Bantu: new data and its relation to Bantu. Circulation draft ms., Cambridge, 20 pp.
sources.note: Comparative wordlists and classification only; no mention of stress, accent or tone. Notes that 'an M.A. thesis on Jar provides a phonological sketch and wordlist' (= Yabilsu 1991).

sources.citation: Gerhardt, Ludwig. 1988. A note on verbal extensions in Jarawan Bantu. Journal of West African Languages 18(2): 3-8.
sources.note: No stress statement. Describes Jaar (=Jar) and Kantana perfective/habitual allomorphy conditioned by stem weight; Table 3 label 'Heavy stress' (p. 6) is a misprint for 'heavy stems'. No tone marking or prosody discussion. (Scan; scanned at 300 dpi,.)
